methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in AI & Software. Range: $29.0B - $312.5B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

private.name: Scale AI
private.rationale: Same sector (AI & Software), same stage (Private), post-money $29B

data.narrative:
Waymo is a late-stage private AI & Software company seeking valuation calibration against a peer set of 1 public and 8 private comparables in autonomous systems and AI infrastructure. The target raised $16B+ and carries a stated valuation of $126B.

Peer-median valuation methodology applies here, drawing from three same-sector, similar-valuation-tier comparables: Palantir (public, $312.5B), Figure AI (Series C, $39.0B), and Scale AI (private, $29.0B). The median across this tranche is $39.0B, with a range of $29.0B to $312.5B. This peer-median approach yields an implied valuation of $39.0B. Given limited methodological breadth (one primary method), triangulation produced a low-to-high range of $33.1B to $44.9B, centered on the $39.0B median.

The $39.0B midpoint sits substantially below Waymo's stated $126B valuation. This gap likely reflects either Waymo's private-market premium relative to staged comparables, founder-specific value attribution, or divergence between stated and defensible valuation. Key uncertainties include capital structure opacities, unmeasured revenue or cash-burn differentials versus peers, and whether the peer set adequately represents frontier autonomous-vehicle economics. Broader triangulation across revenue multiples, discounted cash flow, or additional private benchmarks would strengthen conviction in any final range.
